newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Minimal distillate build seen in API data.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Minimal distillate build seen in API data.

text.p: Tuesday evening's oil inventory data from American Petroleum Institute (API) are expected to show a minimal rise in distillate stocks which are at their lowest level in eight years as exports of heating oil to Europe continue to drain U.S. inventories.

Though refineries are biased towards diesel output rather than heating oil due to better margins, a widening heat crack spread due to soaring prices should boost heat output a little, analysts said. A Reuters survey put the distillate build at 300,000 barrels for the week ended Oct 4.
The estimates ranged from a draw of 500,000 barrels to a build of one million barrels.
"There have been two factors preventing a build, continuing exports to Europe and a disinterest on the part of refiners to make high-sulfur distillate," said Fimat USA Futures analyst Rita Beale.

"But, there was another $1.00 added to the (heating oil) crack last week, so that should encourage a little more production," said Beale. Meanhwile, seasonal maintenance is expected to have cut feverish refinery utilization rates by almost a half percentage point from the current 95.5 percent.
Due to lower run rates, the average estimate for gasoline stocks is for a build of only 600,000 barrels, with the range between down one million to up one million barrels.
The declining run rate is expected have allowed crude stocks to build by around one million barrels, though estimates ranged as high as three million barrels.
Compared to exports, seasonal maintenance was a smaller factor in the paltry build expected in heating oil stocks.
"Exports need to dry up for distillates to build. If that doesn't happen then we can get into real trouble," said William Brown, president of the trading firm W.H. Brown.

"There are no imports coming into the U.S. because of the high price of gas oil (the European equivalent of heating oil)," said a trader. With U.S. heating oil costing less than gas oil, the arbitrage favors exporting.
About 570,000 tonnes of U.S. heating oil was set for export to Europe in October after about 400,000 tonnes of U.S output was exported in September, shipbrokers and traders said.
The strong pace of exports comes at a time when the API data shows heating oil stocks 17.9 million barrels below a year ago.
Total distillate stocks are 18.7 million barrels below a year ago. For the week ended September 27, distillate stocks built a meagre 17,000 barrels.
